summary: M. Yamunacharya worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Bode earned her PhD at the University of Bern under Edouard Müller-Hess and studied widely across Europe. She later lectured at University College London (1909, 1911–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

Madeleine Biardeau was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religion who studied at the École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres and the University of Kerala. She served as a teacher at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).
Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as Professor at the University of Michigan (attested in 1976 and 2006–2009).
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She held posts attested in 2012 at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Fergusson College. He founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and served as Associate Director (1976–1996) and director emeritus of research (~1974–2005) at the AIIS.

Maha Chakri Sirindhorn studied Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned an M.A. in Oriental Epigraphy at Silpakorn University (1977–1979) under Satya Vrat Shastri, alongside studies at Chulalongkorn, Srinakharinwirot, Peking University, and the Asian Institute of Technology.

Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, among others. He was Abbot at Mawlamyine Monastery (1941) and resident teacher/meditation instructor at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha from 1947.
Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He has served at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021).
Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indologist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1882 and 1914).

Mahinda Deegalle works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago, working with Reynolds, Doniger, and Eck. His posts include lecturer at Bath Spa (~2002) and visiting appointments at McGill, Harvard, and Colgate.
Mahiro Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who holds a professorship at Bukkyo University, where he succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.

Maho Iuchi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University (~2002–2008) and served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2010).
Mai Mishiro is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies with posts attested at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2011) and Waseda University (2016).

Takemura is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo, Rissho, Mie, and the University of Tsukuba (~1987–2002), and served as president of Toyo University (2009–2020).
Makio Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Otani University by 2009 and served there as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and staff member (attested 2022).

Makoto Funaoka works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1965–1977), served as part-time lecturer at Komazawa and Open University of Japan, and became professor emeritus at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017).
Makoto Kitada is an Indologist and linguist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Halle. He held a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

Nagai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Toyo (~1914–1944), Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon (~1944–1960), and Kamakura Women's University (~1960–1970).
Makoto Yoshimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1993–2000) and held an assistant professorship at Komazawa University (~2004).
